native_result.query: In the PCA conducted on forms of capital, analyzed in hundred-year time slices, how are the symbolic capital components such as house size, daggers, and hatchets/swords characterized in terms of their values on the first principal component (PC1) and distribution across the second principal component (PC2)?
native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the PCA of the 12 forms of capital across 39 hundred-year slices (BCE 4300-500), the three symbolic-capital indicators — hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert), daggers (ZDolch) and house size (Zhausgr) — load positively and with similar, moderate magnitude on PC1 (30.3% of variance): hatchets/swords +0.30, daggers +0.27, house size +0.23, i.e. they are embedded in the dominant general capital-intensity axis (driven most by copper/gold +0.41, pottery decoration +0.38, depots +0.34) rather than defining it alone. On PC2 (19.5%; PC1+PC2 ~49.8%) the three are split: hatchets/swords (+0.05) and daggers (+0.07) have near-zero loadings (barely expressed on PC2, variation captured by PC1), whereas house size loads distinctly positive (+0.33), aligning with monument-size (+0.39), pottery-form (+0.38), amber (+0.44) and axes/celts (+0.47). House size is thus the symbolic component differentiated along PC2; hatchets/swords and daggers are not. The composite PC2 score oscillates over time (range ~ -3.6 to +2.5; negative in BCE 4300-4100, positive peaks ~BCE 3500-3200 and ~BCE 1400-1100), so PC2 tracks long-run portfolio swings rather than a stable symbolic-capital signature. Overall: moderate, concordant positive PC1 loadings for all three, with a split PC2 distribution in which only house size is meaningfully (positively) expressed.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded capital.csv (39 rows = the 100-yr slices, BCE 4300-500, comma decimal separator); dropped 'group' and 'color' per dataset documentation, leaving the 12 Z-scored capital variables. Data already Z-scored (per-column mean ~0, std ~1); re-standardized to unit variance (ddof=1) and ran a correlation-matrix PCA via eigendecomposition of the 12x12 correlation matrix with numpy (sklearn unavailable), fixing PC sign so the largest-|loading| is positive. Cross-validated eigenvalues/loadings with an independent SVD (identical). Reported eigenvalues, % variance, PC1/PC2 loadings for all 12 vars (emphasis on the 3 symbolic ones) and PC1/PC2 scores of all 39 slices. Caveat: 39 autocorrelated slices for 12 variables makes PC2/higher loadings less stable (bootstrap 5-95% CIs for the PC2 loadings of hatchets/swords and daggers span zero); this does not change the main pattern. Analysis: analysis_pca.py; summary: results_pca.txt.
